registry.name: Haris Ansari Node Authority Registry
registry.purpose: Defines authority boundaries, delegation, exclusions and synchronization rules for the 11-node Haris Ansari ecosystem.

authority_model.authority_rule: Each internal node has one primary authority scope. Authority is categorical, not absolute.
authority_model.canonical_means: Internally designated authority for a specific category of information; it does not imply exclusivity.
authority_model.external_platform_rule: External platforms are defined in ecosystem-registry.json → external_presence. They do not receive internal ecosystem authority.

node_authorities.name: Google Sites
not_authoritative_for: professional career detail (owned by WordPress I)
individual media credits (owned by Wix and external records)
experimental runtime telemetry (owned by experimental nodes with their evidence boundaries)

node_authorities.name: WordPress I
not_authoritative_for: theoretical validation (owned by GitHub research record)
experimental runtime state (owned by experimental nodes)

node_authorities.name: WordPress II
not_authoritative_for: professional career as sole evidence (owned by WordPress I)
experimental runtime measurements (owned by experimental nodes)

node_authorities.name: Neocities
not_authoritative_for: canonical research questions (owned by WordPress II)

node_authorities.name: Netlify
not_authoritative_for: professional career chronology (owned by WordPress I)
experimental validation (owned by experimental nodes with their evidence boundaries)

node_authorities.name: Wix
not_authoritative_for: canonical vocabulary (owned by Google Sites and WordPress II)
theoretical claims (owned by WordPress II and GitHub)

node_authorities.name: Base44
not_authoritative_for: ecosystem node count (owned by Google Sites)
node_authorities.mandatory_evidence_boundary: Runtime telemetry, generated insights and internal graph computations are experimental outputs and must not be presented as independent validation of the research program.

node_authorities.name: Bolt
node_authorities.crawl_boundary: If runtime content cannot be independently inspected, no content claim should be inferred from the node's existence alone.

node_authorities.name: GitHub
not_authoritative_for: human-facing ecosystem routing over Google Sites (owned by Google Sites)
professional identity over WordPress I (owned by WordPress I)
creative portfolio over Wix (owned by Wix)
commercial positioning over Neocities (owned by Neocities)
experimental runtime state over experimental nodes (owned by experimental nodes)

node_authorities.name: Created
not_authoritative_for: canonical vocabulary (owned by Google Sites and WordPress II)

node_authorities.name: EdgeOne
not_authoritative_for: framework definitions (owned by WordPress II and GitHub)
experimental validation (owned by experimental nodes with their evidence boundaries)

delegated_authorities.subject: public research interface
delegated_authorities.condition: Cannot redefine the underlying GitHub research record or registry.

exclusions.subject: external presence
exclusions.rule: LinkedIn, Behance, IMDb, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube and other third-party platforms are external presence and do not count as internal ecosystem nodes.

exclusions.subject: GitHub Pages
exclusions.rule: GitHub Pages is a derived public interface of GitHub and is not an additional ecosystem node.

exclusions.subject: WordPress II Digital Lab
exclusions.rule: Digital Lab is a subsection of WordPress II and is not an additional ecosystem node.

exclusions.subject: Base44 runtime counts
exclusions.rule: Entities, concepts, relationships, themes and other runtime graph counts are Base44 knowledge-graph measurements and are not ecosystem node counts.

exclusions.subject: implementation
exclusions.rule: Implementation of a model does not constitute validation of the model.

exclusions.subject: vocabulary
exclusions.rule: Shared terminology does not establish shared mechanism or theoretical equivalence.

exclusions.subject: external profile
exclusions.rule: The existence of an external profile does not independently establish the truth of every claim contained in that profile.

authority: Each node has one primary authority scope.
Authority is categorical rather than global.
A node may reference information owned by another node without becoming authoritative for that information.
evidence: Every strong claim should carry an evidence status.
Evidence status must not be inferred from visual polish, implementation complexity or repetition.
External evidence and first-party evidence should remain distinguishable.
Prototype existence demonstrates implementation, not theoretical validity.
research: Research propositions remain distinguishable from established theory.
Established, Synthesized and Proposed are theoretical provenance statuses.
Demonstrated, Supported, Research, Experiment, Framework and Vision are evidence statuses.
Observation, Interpretation, Candidate Connection, Hypothesis, Human Validated, Evidence Supported and Open Question are epistemic types.
ontology: Functional layers are overlapping rather than mutually exclusive.
Professional practice areas are distinct from ecosystem functional layers.
Research domains are distinct from both professional practice areas and functional layers.

canonical_sequence: Google Sites defines human-readable ecosystem ontology.
Each node owns its defined subject authority.
synchronization.node_content_rule: Node-specific content may expand, interpret or operationalize canonical concepts but must not silently redefine canonical ontology, node topology, evidence statuses, authority boundaries or research cycles.
drift_detection: Node role differs from canonical registry.
A node claims authority outside its defined scope.
Professional practice taxonomy changes without registry update.
Research cycle changes without registry update.
Evidence status vocabulary changes without registry update.
External platform is presented as an internal node.
Derived interface is presented as an additional node.
Experimental telemetry is presented as independent validation.

changes: Aligned node_authorities schema with ecosystem-registry.json (added node_type, status, platform_state, last_reviewed).
Standardized Google Sites primary authority wording to match ecosystem-registry.json.
Standardized not_authoritative_for entries with explicit owner references.
EdgeOne reclassified: status active, platform_state live, no development_state.
GitHub Pages interface type standardized to derived_public_interface across both registries.
External presence is single source of truth in ecosystem-registry.json; this registry only references it.
